summary: Iteration 4 hard-paywall + reminders. Backend: 17/17 paywall tests PASS. /workouts/today, /workouts/complete, /workouts/rate, /meals/plans, /chat all correctly return 402 for users without active sub. /auth/me, /profile (PUT), /calories, /progress/weight (POST/GET), /progress/weekly, /subscription/* all return 200. Subscription status correctly returns active=false for new users. Stripe checkout still creates valid sessions. Frontend: CRITICAL bug found and patched in /app/frontend/src/AuthContext.tsx — `subscription` state, `setSubscription` setter, and `refreshSubscription` function were referenced (in type, signOut, Provider value) but NEVER declared, causing ReferenceError that broke the entire app on first render. Added missing useState + useCallback. After fix, app loads correctly. Verified: unauth user → /auth/login redirect ✅. Login as test@cy.com (profile complete, no sub) → /subscribe redirect ✅. /subscribe screen renders all 3 plans (£3.99/£19.99/£34.99), BEST VALUE badge on yearly, SUBSCRIBE NOW button (testID subscribe-btn) visible. Zero console errors after fix. Did NOT complete real Stripe payment per instructions, so tabs-layout defense-in-depth redirect, onboarding→/subscribe transition, and setting-reminders toggle were not exercised end-to-end (require active sub).

ui_bugs.issue: ReferenceError: subscription is not defined — `subscription` state, setSubscription, and refreshSubscription were referenced in AuthCtx type, signOut, and Provider value but never declared via useState/useCallback. Entire app crashed on first render (red-screen). PATCHED in this iteration by adding `const [subscription, setSubscription] = useState<SubscriptionStatus | null>(null)` and a refreshSubscription callback that GETs /api/subscription/status.

critical_code_review_comments: AuthContext.tsx shipped with three undefined identifiers in the Provider value — this should have been caught by TypeScript strict mode or a smoke render. Recommend enabling `noUnusedLocals` + `strict` in tsconfig and adding a render-smoke test that mounts AuthProvider.

/app/frontend/src/notifications.ts uses Notifications.scheduleNotificationAsync trigger object {hour, minute, repeats:true}. expo-notifications v0.30+ requires `type: 'daily'` or SchedulableTriggerInputTypes.DAILY. Without it, the daily reminder may not fire on native iOS/Android. Worth verifying on a real device.

rca_of_issue: AuthContext.tsx had three undefined identifiers (subscription, setSubscription, refreshSubscription) referenced in the Provider value, signOut handler, and AuthCtx type. Root cause: incomplete implementation — the type contract was extended for iteration 3/4 subscription state, but the corresponding useState and useCallback bodies were never added inside AuthProvider. Symptom: ReferenceError on first render → entire app red-screened → no UI testable at all. Fix: declared `const [subscription, setSubscription] = useState<SubscriptionStatus|null>(null)` and `const refreshSubscription = useCallback(async () => GET /api/subscription/status, persist to AsyncStorage, return status)` inside AuthProvider. Verified app now boots, redirects unauth→login, and authenticated-no-sub users→/subscribe.
